indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.2.1: Know common diseases of humans, causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
indicator.objective: Identify some common diseases that affect the skin and their causes

skills.description: State simple causes of skin diseases
Describe ways to prevent skin diseases
Recognise simple signs of skin diseases

misconceptions: Skin diseases are caused by curses or witchcraft.
You can catch skin diseases just by looking at someone who has them.
Ringworm is caused by a worm or an insect.
Only poor people get skin diseases.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common skin disease?
hints: It causes a round, itchy patch.
questions.explanation: Ringworm is a common skin disease that causes itchy, round patches on the skin.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any sickness is a skin disease.

questions.stem: What is a common sign of a skin disease?
hints: You want to scratch the spot.
questions.explanation: Itching is a common sign of a skin disease.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse skin disease symptoms with other illnesses.

questions.stem: What can cause skin diseases?
questions.explanation: Dirt and germs can cause skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think skin diseases are caused by other actions like eating.

questions.stem: How can you prevent skin diseases?
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly with soap helps prevent skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link hygiene to disease prevention.

questions.stem: Which of these is a skin disease that gives red, itchy spots?
hints: It causes a rash on the skin.
questions.explanation: Measles is a disease that causes red spots on the skin.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think malaria is a skin disease.

questions.stem: Ama is wearing dirty clothes that she has not washed for days. What skin problem might she get?
hints: Dirty clothes can irritate the skin.
Sweat and dirt stay on the skin.
questions.explanation: Wearing dirty clothes can trap sweat and dirt, causing heat rashes or itching.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect dirty clothes to skin issues.

questions.stem: Why should you not share a towel with a friend who has ringworm?
options: You can catch the disease from the towel
hints: Germs can stay on the towel.
questions.explanation: You can catch skin diseases like ringworm by sharing towels because germs can spread from the infected person.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sharing is always good, without considering germs.

questions.stem: Kwame has an itchy, red patch on his arm. What type of disease is this?
questions.explanation: An itchy, red patch on the skin is a sign of a skin disease.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not identify skin conditions correctly.

questions.stem: What causes ringworm?
hints: It is caused by something you cannot see.
questions.explanation: Ringworm is caused by a fungus (germ), not a real worm, even though it is called ringworm.
questions.misconception: Pupils often think ringworm is caused by a real worm.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a skin disease?
hints: Which one is carried by mosquitoes?
It causes fever and body pain.
questions.explanation: Malaria is not a skin disease; it is caused by mosquito bites and affects the blood.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse diseases that cause fever with skin diseases.

questions.stem: Name one thing that can cause skin diseases.
hints: What happens if you don't bathe?
What do you catch if you are dirty?
questions.explanation: Dirt, germs, and poor hygiene can cause skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may answer with unrelated causes.

questions.stem: What should you do every day to prevent skin diseases?
questions.explanation: You should bathe every day with soap and water to prevent skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say you only need to bathe when dirty.

questions.stem: Kofi sees a circular, red, itchy patch on his little brother's skin. What should he do?
options: Tell their parents to take him to a clinic
Ignore it because it is not serious
hints: A health worker can give medicine.
questions.explanation: Kofi should tell their parents so his brother can be taken to a clinic for treatment to prevent it from spreading.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think skin diseases are not serious and ignore them.

questions.stem: Why is it important to wash your clothes regularly?
options: To prevent skin diseases like heat rashes
To make the clothes change colour
questions.explanation: Washing clothes regularly prevents sweat, dirt, and germs from staying on your skin, which helps prevent skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize dirty clothes affect skin health.

questions.stem: Which statement about skin diseases is TRUE?
options: You can catch skin diseases by looking at someone
You can prevent skin diseases by keeping your body clean
Only poor people get skin diseases
Skin diseases are caused by curses
hints: Skin diseases are caused by germs, not looks.
questions.explanation: Skin diseases can be prevented by keeping your body clean, not by looking at someone.
questions.misconception: Pupils often hold beliefs about curses or poverty causing diseases.

questions.stem: Explain why sharing personal items like towels and sponges can cause skin diseases.

criteria.description: States that germs can pass from one person to another
States that this can cause a skin infection

questions.explanation: Sharing towels and sponges can spread germs from an infected person to a healthy person, causing skin diseases.

questions.stem: Role-play a scenario showing how you can prevent a skin disease (e.g., bathing, not sharing a towel).

criteria.description: Demonstrates a valid prevention action (e.g., washing hands, bathing)
Shows understanding of why this prevents the disease

hints: What do you do before sharing?
questions.explanation: This tests the practical understanding of preventing skin diseases through hygiene.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Ringworm is caused by a worm.' Why is she wrong?
options: Ringworm is caused by germs (a fungus), not a worm
Ringworm is caused by eating too much
Ringworm is caused by a curse
hints: Can you see a worm in ringworm?
It is a germ that causes it.
questions.explanation: Ringworm is caused by a fungus (germ), not a real worm, even though the name has 'worm' in it.
questions.misconception: Pupils often think ringworm is caused by a literal worm.

questions.stem: Write down two ways you can prevent skin diseases at school.

criteria.description: Names one correct way (e.g., bathing regularly, not sharing towels, washing hands)

hints: What do you do in the bathroom?
questions.explanation: You can prevent skin diseases by bathing, washing hands, and not sharing personal items.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher what you should do if you notice an itchy rash on your skin.

criteria.description: States they should tell a parent or teacher
States they should seek medical attention or go to a clinic

questions.explanation: If you notice a rash, you should tell a trusted adult and seek medical attention to get proper treatment.
